day_summary: Juneteenth — US equity markets closed. No official NVDA trading. Last close: $208.82 on June 18 (+2.04%), the first close above the 50-DMA ($206.74) since the FOMC dump. Pre-market / extended-hours trading on June 19 shows NVDA at ~$210.33, session range $206.50–$211.39 — thin holiday liquidity, no institutional participation, limited informational value. Night update — gate status revision: VIX confirmed at 16.40 on June 18 close (not 17.0 as initially reported) — the VIX gate (<17) IS NOW CLEARED. Combined with SPX at 7,500 (gate cleared), TWO of THREE conditional-add gates are now cleared as of June 18 close. Only the DXY gate (<100) remains unmet — DXY hit a Juneteenth intraday one-year high of 101.13, settling at 100.79. The conditional-add framework going into Monday June 22: (1) VIX gate: CLEARED (16.40); (2) SPX gate: CLEARED (7,500); (3) DXY gate: UNMET (100.79 — needs to confirm below 100.00 on Monday June 22 close). The setup into Monday is more constructive than the morning brief indicated: a single DXY confirmation below 100 on June 22 activates the $205–$215 conditional add. The DXY direction on June 22 open (Hormuz commercial traffic flowing, Switzerland talks postponed not canceled) is the week's binary trigger. Jensen Huang confirmed for the NVIDIA Annual Meeting online June 24 at 9 AM PT — first post-FOMC management commentary on AI capex trajectory remains the week's primary catalyst. Jensen completed an 18-day Taiwan–South Korea trip in which NVIDIA committed ~$150B annual spending in Taiwan and struck deals with Korean firms on robotics, memory, and AI. Q2 FY27 earnings scheduled ~August 26 at ~$91B revenue consensus.
long_pnl: holders from the June 15–16 add zone ($211–$214) remain ~1.0–2.0% offside; pre-market ~$210.33 is in the add zone on thin liquidity but no institutional confirmation; the thesis requires two gates to clear on June 22 (VIX <17 AND DXY <100); DXY moving to 100.75 on Juneteenth makes the DXY gate less likely to clear on June 22 open
short_pnl: bears capped at $208.82 with no new downside to trade today; DXY rising to 100.75 is the bear's best friend — if the gate fails to clear on June 22 (DXY holds above 100) the conditional-add remains suspended indefinitely and the range-bound bear thesis extends; Annual Meeting June 24 is the next short-cover risk

Two of three conditional-add gates are now cleared: (1) VIX gate: CLEARED (16.40 < 17); (2) SPX gate: CLEARED (7,500 > 7,460); (3) DXY gate: UNMET — DXY hit 101.13 intraday one-year high on Juneteenth FX, settled 100.79. The Annual Meeting June 24 is the event-driven override: Jensen Huang's direct commentary on AI capex resilience and the Rubin ramp can trigger the add regardless of the DXY level. Stop at $195 daily close unchanged.

The Annual Meeting June 24 introduces a new layer: if Jensen Huang explicitly addresses the rate environment and signals AI capex acceleration, the add executes regardless of the macro gates (the fundamental signal overrides the technical gates when management provides direct guidance).

outlook.short_term: Gate-dependent; DXY is the remaining blocker and is worsening. The June 18 technical confirmation (close above 50-DMA at $208.82) is valid but the macro regime is not cooperating: DXY at 100.75 on Juneteenth FX means the first gate a June 22 trader needs to check (DXY <100) is further from clearing than on June 18 evening. June 22 is the diagnostic: (1) If DXY opens June 22 below 100 AND VIX closes below 17 → conditional add activates, execute $205–$215 with stop $195; (2) If DXY holds above 100 on June 22 → add SUSPENDED, hold position, reassess after Annual Meeting June 24. The Annual Meeting is the event that can override a partial macro-gate failure — Jensen Huang's direct commentary on AI capex and the Rubin/Blackwell ramp is the primary catalyst regardless of the rate environment.
outlook.long_term: Intact and unchanged. The FOMC hawkish shock creates a near-term multiple headwind (higher discount rate on ~30x P/E), not a structural change. Jensen Huang's $150B Taiwan supply commitment, SK Hynix locked through 2030, $91B Q2 revenue consensus, $299 average analyst PT, and the AI capex supercycle are all fundamental drivers independent of the Warsh dot plot. Q2 FY27 earnings ~August 26 is the next conviction anchor.

bull_case: Annual Meeting June 24 is the week's event-driven catalyst — Jensen Huang is the one person who can override the macro-gate framework with direct commentary on AI capex resilience; any signal on the Rubin ramp, HBM4 demand trajectory, or explicit message to long-term investors about the rate-neutral nature of AI spending could trigger a PT revision cycle regardless of the DXY level.

DXY at 100.75 is above 100 but could reverse quickly: the Iran ceasefire macro pathway (Hormuz reopening → oil structurally lower → CPI relief in July → Fed hawkish dots require revision → DXY peaks) is still in motion; if the first Hormuz transit data (expected within 30 days) shows oil supply increasing, DXY falls and the gate clears.

SK Hynix extended to ₩2,764,000 (+2.94%) on June 19 KOSPI — three consecutive ATH sessions confirm that the AI memory supply chain (NVDA's primary fundamental input) is in structural acceleration; this is the best leading indicator that NVDA's own fundamental thesis has not been affected by the FOMC.

Jensen's 18-day Asia trip ($150B Taiwan commitment, Korean robotics/AI deals) demonstrates that NVDA is building the supply chain for the next 5 years — the scale of these commitments makes the FOMC rate path a secondary consideration for the AI-infrastructure supercycle investment case.
bear_case: DXY at 100.75 on Juneteenth FX — moving in the WRONG direction on the only day the equity market can't respond; if DXY holds above 100 all week (which is possible if Warsh's 3.8% dot median reaffirms Fed policy is data-dependent and June PCE/CPI doesn't provide relief), the conditional-add is suspended through the earnings period.

VIX at 17.0 is technically at the gate but the 8-of-9 post-FOMC weakness pattern means the next 5 days (June 22–26) are the historically weakest period; VIX at 17.0 could easily re-expand to 18–19 on any adverse macro headline (Fed speaker, 30Y testing 5.00%) before June 24 Annual Meeting.

The 30Y at 4.93% approaching 5.00% is the regime's most dangerous near-term trigger: a sustained close above 5.00% would simultaneously void the NVDA conditional-add framework, compress NVDA's multiple, and generate institutional bond-to-equity reallocation headwinds.

BTC stop execution on June 19 is a risk-sentiment read: if BTC closes below $63,500 at UTC midnight June 19 (Day 2 of stop clock), it confirms the FOMC hawkish regime is more persistent than the Iran ceasefire can offset; this has historically dragged AI semis lower in the 5–10 days following a crypto break-down.
